card.title: Mass Defect, Packing Fraction, Binding Energy per Nucleon

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **mass defect** Δm = [Zm_p + (A−Z)m_n] − M is the shortfall between the free nucleons' total mass and the actual nuclear mass (NEB 2023, 3m) — bound nuclei weigh less than their parts. Its energy equivalent, **BE = Δmc²** (Δm × 931.5 MeV per u), is the energy to dismantle the nucleus; the **packing fraction** Δm/A and **BE per nucleon** measure stability.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Δm = Zm_p + (A−Z)m_n − M - BE = Δmc² = Δm × 931.5 MeV (u) - Packing fraction f = (M − A)/A - BE/A peaks ≈ 8.8 MeV at ⁵⁶Fe

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Atomic vs Nuclear Mass: Atomic mass includes electrons; for BE calculation use nuclear mass. Electron masses cancel if using atomic masses consistently (Z electrons on both sides).  ·  BE/A for Stability: Compare BE/A, not total BE — total BE always increases with A but stability depends on per-nucleon value.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Mass defect is the difference between the sum of the masses of the individual nucleons and the actual nuclear mass; binding energy is its energy equivalent."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Helium-4*** — Δm = 0.0305 u → BE ≈ 28.4 MeV, 7.1 MeV per nucleon.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Δm is positive for bound nuclei** — the whole weighs LESS than the sum of its parts.  ·  **Iron-56 is the stability peak** — energy is released moving toward it from either side.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Missing Mass That Holds Nuclei Together Weigh a helium nucleus: its parts weigh more than the whole. The missing 0.76% — the **mass defect** — left as binding energy, is the glue of every nucleus and the ledger behind fission and fusion.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023) ### 2.1 Mass defect **Mass defect** is the difference between the sum of the masses of the individual nucleons and the actual mass of the nucleus (NEB 2023, 3m): $$\Delta m = \left[Zm_p + (A-Z)m_n\right] - M_{nucleus}$$ — always positive for bound nuclei: the assembled nucleus weighs *less* than its parts.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Sketch the BE/A curve with the iron peak labelled — it carries marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Binding energy is the missing mass** — the energy that would be needed to unbuild the nucleus.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Δm = [Zm_p + (A−Z)m_n] − M; BE = Δm × 931.5 MeV per u; BE/A peaks ~8.8 MeV at A ≈ 56.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Fusion in stars and fission in reactors both climb the BE/A curve toward iron.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Packing Fraction Sign: Negative packing fraction means mass < A (mass defect) — bound nucleus. Positive means unstable relative to nucleons.  ·  Verified PYQ: mass defect + binding energy relation (2023, 3m).  ·  Why does uranium fission release energy if heavy nuclei are "full"?
